text: Every security control Oakmere has built so far lives as code in the team's own repository -- and that repository has never had a security gate of its own.

This lesson adds two required checks: a secrets scan that blocks a pull request if it finds a credential committed in plaintext, and an infrastructure scan that blocks risky configurations before they merge.

On their very first real run, the scans catch two live issues -- a leaked threat-intel API key, and a draft network rule with the exact same wildcard mistake the team had just spent a whole lesson fixing elsewhere.
Both are blocked before they ever reach production. High and critical findings stop the merge outright; lower-severity findings get tracked without creating friction the team would route around.
Next: an alert that should have fired on a real compromise, and didn't.
